title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
why: Studies Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI): continuing an existing harness-optimization method across compatible benchmarks or policy models, with the task model treated as a policy that can change. Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) is attached to the harness optimizer rather than the task-solving policy, grouping edits by recurring harness problem and recording rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context so later attempts can reuse or revise earlier harness edits instead of starting from the harness alone.
mechanism: A memory for the harness optimizer (not the task policy) that stores grouped harness-edit histories with rationales, predicted vs observed outcomes, and evaluation context, so harness optimization can continue when the benchmark or policy model changes.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): experiments across four domains; SIM achieves higher final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation in cross-dataset and pairwise continuation settings (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
why: Targets self-improving coding agents that iteratively modify their own executable implementations. Instead of evaluate-and-select (repeatedly running evolved agents on downstream tasks to decide which lineage continues), ELITE (Explore-then-Integrate) proposes diverse focused improvements, implements them independently, and integrates implementation mechanisms rather than selecting a single exploratory child—so the evolution loop does not depend on downstream task evaluation inside the loop. Directly in the Darwin Gödel Machine / coding-agent RSI line.
mechanism: Evaluation-free RSI for coding agents: at each generation, diverse focused improvements are implemented independently and their mechanisms are integrated into the lineage, avoiding downstream-task evaluate-and-select inside the evolution loop.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): asks whether coding agents can self-improve without downstream task evaluation in the loop; compares ELITE to evaluate-and-select self-improving coding agents (benchmark names and numbers are not fully stated in the abs excerpt; 32 pages / 14 figures claimed in comments).

title: Read, Route, Patch: Robust Test-Time Evolution for LLM Agents
why: Test-time evolution of LLM agents that treats candidate harnesses as the object of improvement: Trident addresses memory-retrieval, behavioral-redundancy, and whole-harness-rewrite failure modes with boundary-aware memory reading, diversity-aware candidate routing, and order-aware insertion-based harness updating (a patch rather than a full rewrite). Compared on text-game, web, and coding benchmarks against non-learning, memory, reflection, and automated prompt-optimization baselines including APEX, with frozen backbones.
mechanism: Test-time harness evolution via (i) boundary-aware memory reading, (ii) diversity-aware routing among candidate harnesses, and (iii) order-aware insertion-based updates that patch the harness instead of rewriting it whole.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated on five benchmarks spanning text games, web interaction, and coding, with qwen-32B, mistral-small-3.2-24B, and gpt-oss-20B. Trident is reported as best average vs non-learning, memory-based, reflection-based, and automated prompt optimization baselines; vs strongest baseline APEX, relative average gains of 30.7%, 30.8%, and 38.3% on the three backbones.

title: MetaAct: Self-Evolving Executable Action Constraints for Embodied Language Agents
why: Moves self-evolution of embodied language agents from textual guidance to executable action constraints. MetaAct synthesizes Grounded Executable Action Rules (GEAR) from execution feedback: each rule is a typed specification compiled into a deterministic guard and validated offline by trajectory replay without extra model calls or environment interactions, so admitted constraints are retained and enforced.
mechanism: Self-evolving executable action constraints: execution feedback is turned into typed GEAR rules, compiled to deterministic guards, and validated offline by trajectory replay before being retained and enforced at action time.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across four benchmarks MetaAct improves task performance; on ScienceWorld and WebShop, violations drop from 70% to 0% and 40% to 1%, with score gains of +10.1 and +8.0.

title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
why: Jointly evolves a curriculum harness and an execution harness around frozen foundation models: the curriculum proposer uses accumulated capability evidence to invent practice, and the execution harness admits reusable revisions (skills, planning procedures, recovery). Alternating updates hold one side fixed while the other changes, and admitted challenges become fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions—co-evolving evaluators/curricula plus a retained execution harness.
mechanism: Adversarial co-evolution of a curriculum harness (challenge proposal from accumulated capability evidence) and an execution harness (reusable skill/planning/recovery revisions) around frozen foundation models, with alternation and snapshot challenges for comparing revisions.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, 74.0% success, +15.0 points over the initial deployment and +13.5 over direct execution by its VLA controller. Case studies mention evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
why: Natural-language optimization of an agent's retained policy artifacts (system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations) posed as constrained combinatorial search over a block-structured edit graph. Sections that encode contracts stay immutable while other blocks are legitimate optimization targets, addressing global rewrites, beam collapse, and bloat that arise when the artifact is treated as a single editable string.
mechanism: Structured NLO / prompt evolution: optimization is constrained combinatorial search over selectively mutable blocks of a natural-language policy document, with per-block mutability so contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, formats) cannot drift.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): frames three recurrent NLO failure modes and maps each to a formal guarantee (per-block mutability and further guarantees whose details sit past the listing excerpt). Specific benchmark numbers are not in the abs excerpt.

title: Synapse: Optimizing Natural-Language Agent Skills through Program Repair
why: Optimizes reusable natural-language agent skills without updating model parameters by casting skill edits as generate-and-validate program repair. A deterministic compiler maps recognized skill constructs into SkIR, a source-linked IR; traces plus control-flow and dependence relations localize faults, propose typed mutations, and select related repair tests (including previously passing ones). Accepted patches are written back to mapped source spans, recompiled, and validated so untargeted instruction spans are preserved.
mechanism: Skill optimization as program repair: NL skills are compiled to a source-linked IR (SkIR); execution traces and structural dependence drive typed mutations and test selection; accepted patches are written back and recompiled without changing model weights.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on DocVQA and LiveMath with three execution models, Synapse improves task success over SkillOpt by 3.74–4.54 and 2.40–4.00 points, and outperforms Trace2Skill and SkillBoost in all six settings. Replacing SkIR-based repair and test screening with constrained text editing screened only on failing tests lowers DocVQA success by 2.40 and 2.67 points for two models. In two recorded repair runs, structural relations add tests for 23 of 37 patches.

title: Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
why: Holds both the skill's capability ceiling and the model's parameters fixed, and adapts a modular agent skill (instructions, code, and resources) so a weaker agent can execute it. Strong and weak trajectories are abstracted into typed execution structures to close the gap where a frontier-authored skill helps a strong model but transfers poorly—or hurts—on a weaker one. This is retained skill-library adaptation, not weight training.
mechanism: Skill transfer: with model parameters and the skill's capability ceiling held fixed, the skill artifact itself is adapted so a specific weaker agent can execute it, using typed execution structures abstracted from strong vs weak trajectories.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): formalizes the strong-to-weak skill gap (a strong model realizes a large gain; a weak model realizes little and can do worse than no skill). Experimental numbers sit past the listing/abs excerpt.

title: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
why: Coding agents synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, then factor the controller into an environment interpreter (models, memory, skills) and a rule program, and evolve a reusable goal compiler that maps structured tasks into new rule programs. The resulting programs act with zero inference-time model calls. Continuation-scored feedback and a fixed machine with an editable program turn a single-task competent policy into a transferable one—program/harness evolution, not weight training.
mechanism: Continuation-guided LLM evolution of program policies, then factorization into a reusable interpreter plus a goal compiler Cθ that maps structured tasks to new rule programs; compiled programs run without inference-time LLM calls.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): in Craftax, refinements via episode-level feedback stall at <1% final-level arrival, whereas with the feedback cascade the optimized policy reaches the final stage 50% of the time (28% final boss defeats). Across five independent compiler searches trained only on short tasks, compilers transfer zero-shot to longer tasks without task-specific tuning or inference-time LLM calls.

title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
why: Starts from a negative finding that naive cross-task memory can make an agent worse than memoryless ReAct, then supplies per-action credit assignment and an explicit lifecycle for retained procedural entries. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a critic scores the realized outcome, writes a procedural entry with a binary reward and a reflection, and updates a scalar utility online (noisy-OR) used jointly with similarity at retrieval—retained procedural memory, not weight training.
mechanism: Expectation-grounded procedural memory: per-action expected-outcome commitments, a critic that credits the action that earned the outcome, retained entries with reward plus reflection, and an online utility used with similarity at retrieval, plus an explicit entry lifecycle.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than memoryless ReAct in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. AdMem is presented as addressing those failures (further numbers sit past the listing excerpt). Comments: NeurIPS 2026 workshop 'Agents in the Wild'.

title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
why: A negative-result / safety audit of LLM critics that steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement. Isolates the critic's marginal effect with a four-arm audit and fault injection, and reports that a naive critic can drive search below the no-critic random-search floor—exactly the kind of critic-in-the-loop evaluation this radar collects for self-improving / prompt-optimization loops.
mechanism: Audit of critic-in-the-loop search (prompt optimization, self-refinement, agentic AutoML): four-arm isolation of the critic's marginal effect plus controlled fault injection to measure when directional critic errors consume finite search opportunities.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; magnitude varies with dataset, frontier, and budget. Non-directional errors are nearly costless under best-so-far search, whereas directional errors consume search opportunities. Comments: accepted at KDD 2027 Research track.

title: EfficientSkill: Learning Skills for Token-Efficient Multi-Turn Agents
why: A two-step reflective skill optimizer for multi-turn agents: first discover a reliable skill without token penalties, then warm-start accuracy-guarded pruning from that skill to compress instructions, bound agent turns, and offload reusable code into workspace utilities. Addresses prompt bloat in skill-evolution methods such as EvoSkill while keeping the retained skill artifact as the object of improvement.
mechanism: Two-step skill optimization: unconstrained discovery of a reliable skill, then accuracy-guarded pruning that compresses instructions, bounds turns, and offloads reusable code into workspace utilities with zero implementation-prompt cost.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): four frontier, mid-tier, and open-weight models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench. EfficientSkill cuts output tokens vs unconstrained EvoSkill on 11 of 12 configurations (by up to 80%) while raising mean accuracy on every benchmark, including +14.3 and +17.5 points on SpreadsheetBench with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.
